w: Swamishri travelled to Dharampur, the native town of Kushal Kunvarba sanctified by Shriji Maharaj. In the evening, a mammoth gathering of 7,000 tribals availed of the darshan and blessings of Swamishri.

In the evening at 6.10 p.m., Swamishri, after visiting the holy places sanctified by Shriji Maharaj during His visit to the palace of queen Kushal Kunvarba 183 years ago, addressed a gathering of 7,000 tribals. After the preliminary welcoming ceremony, tribal folk dances and speeches by dignitaries, Swamishri blessed the occasion. "I congratulate all of you who have come from far and wide places to this spiritual assembly. In this world there are so many different types of benefits, but the benefit one will gain here will elevate you, bring inner progress and salvation. You will also experience the highest bliss because God is the very home of happiness.

"God and His incarnations and holy sadhus have blessed us so that our lives as individuals, as a family, a society and a nation can become better and happier. And to be a recipient of this benefit, that is why the holy sadhus constantly travel for the benefit of all..."
ph: Swamishri at the assembly, Dharampur, 3 May 1999

w: After completing his morning puja, Swamishri worshipped the canvas murtis to be installed at the new Akshar Purushottam Mandir at Bhadut village.
In his evening blessings, Swamishri stressed upon the extent of endeavoring in one's occupation to satisfy one's physical needs.

"One should strive to earn money according to one's needs. One should not remain steeped in business or work for the entire twelve months. Foxes and wolves kill their prey even if they are not hungry, whereas the lion is an animal of integrity. It kills only when it is hungry....If you eat the required quantity of food then it will be easily digested. Similarly, one should earn according to one's daily, yearly or lifetime needs. After earning enough, one should then engage in doing bhajan. But like the fox and the wolf, to eat and drink, party and travel around all day is improper and wrong."

A special assembly of 400 youths between the ages of 23 and 35 was held in the mandir hall in the morning. The theme of the assembly was ‘Pride for Satsang’. Viveksagar Swami addressed the youths about the glory of Shri Harikrishna Maharaj. Finally Swamishri blessed the youths explaining about having pride for one’s family, country and Satsang. In conclusion the youths honored Shri Harikrishna Maharaj.
In the evening assembly the youths performed a drama ‘Be a Proud Satsangi’. The assembly was capped with Swamishri’s blessings.
“Do you eat and drink?” Swamishri asked a youth in Gujarati.
“What?” the Gujarati youth, not knowing the language, asked.
“Are you vegetarian?” Swamishri asked in English.
“Occasionally I take meat.”
The dialogue continued with the help of a translator.

“If someone were to beat you, wouldn’t your parents be hurt? And if someone were to hurt your parents, wouldn’t you be pained? Animals also love their children. To be compassionate is the duty of a human being. And secondly, cows, buffaloes and oxen offer so much service to us. How would it be to kill those that serve us!” Swamishri’s words touched the youth.
“What do you feel?” Swamishri asked.
“You are right,” the youth agreed.
“Take a pledge today that you will be a vegetarian.”
“My mother is vegetarian, my sister is vegetarian. So there won’t be a problem. Now I’ll be a vegetarian,” the boy pledged.
Swamishri blessed the youth.

ds.t: "From now on I will be vegetarian"
w: During the meetings a youth came. Pramukh Swami Maharaj's first question was, "Do you eat and drink anything?"
"What?" Not understanding, the youth asked back.
Swamishri asked, "Do you drink alcohol? Do you eat meat?"

His expression showed that he had not understood anything. He was Gujarati, but he has been forgetting the language, and in the same way he has been drifting away from the culture and its values. This is the condition of youths outside satsang here. Swamishri saw that he did not understand anything. So he himself asked him in English, "Are you vegetarian?"
Understanding a little, he said, "Sometimes I take meat."

Swamishri finished the rest with an interpreter. Swamishri said, "If someone hurt you, would your parents feel pain or not? If someone hurt your parents, would you feel pain or not? In the same way, animals too love their young. It is our dharma as humans to have compassion. And besides, how much service the cow, buffalo or bullock gives us! If we kill those who serve us, what would you call that?"
These values of feeling and compassion were having the desired effect on the youth. His tone kept softening. He said only this much: "Yes."
In this "yes" was the echo of his slightly melted heart. Swamishri caught that echo and asked, "How did you feel about this?"
"Take a vow today that from now on you will remain vegetarian."
Swamishri explained to him with such love that he became firm in his mind. He said, "My mother is vegetarian. My sister is vegetarian. No problem. From now on I too will remain vegetarian."
Only a mighty warrior like Swamishri can succeed in changing this nature of the new generation here.

ds.t: The golden age in the age of Kali!
w: A youth came with his father to meet Pramukh Swami Maharaj. He had tilak chandlo on his forehead. He did dandvat to Swamishri, touched his feet and sat down. As soon as he saw Swamishri, he said, weeping, "Bapa! Please do something about our father."
"What is wrong with your father?"
He said, "He takes alcohol and meat."

Swamishri sat up a little. Folding his outstretched legs into a half cross-legged position, he said to the father, "Listen to this son of yours. Does anyone get such a son in this age? You should be the one to reform him; instead, God is inspiring him and speaking to you. Crores of people live without eating meat and so on. Why can't you? Decide. Maharaj Himself has entered this boy. Believe that."

While Swamishri was explaining, the youth was sobbing uncontrollably. This is the power of satsang. In a foreign land, such a sight is extremely rare except in the satsang community. Here, through the power of satsang, the Ganga flows backwards. This is Swamishri's golden page. The father melted and took a vow not to take alcohol or meat from then on.
Swamishri said, "Keep this vow now until the end of your life. And to get the strength to keep the vow, come to the mandir and keep the company of the sadhus."

st.t: Satsang Asmita - Young Yuvak/Yuvtis Assembly - Monday 3 May 2004
w: Satsang Asmita was the subject of the Young Yuvak-Yuvati assembly in the presence of Pramukh Swami Maharaj as a large assembly gathered in the Haveli for the morning programme. Shri Harikrishna Maharaj ‘Suvarna Tula’ festival was the central event, offering the youngsters a unique opportunity to offer their devotion to Shri Harikrishna Maharaj, the sacred image of Bhagwan Swaminarayan.
As the sadhus narrated various incidents, the collection of touching memories and the acute devotion offered by Swamishri inspired sadhus and devotees alike.

Swamishri opened his blessings with the emphasis on satsang asmita, discussing the pride individuals exhibit towards one’s nation, family, possessions and status; for devotees, however, the pride of this satsang is of utmost important. Urging youths to control their minds and remain within the roots of this satsang, Swamishri underlined the importance of adhering to one’s religious principles, avoiding unsuitable company, which tarnishes the mind. An episode from Maharaj’s life was referenced, where a young boy presented a watermelon to Maharaj after a considerable battle with his mind, overcoming his desire to consume the fruit en route.

Swamishri encouraged the youths to remain strong and firm. Swamishri concluded his address by asking the inspired youths to remain humble, and to imbibe the true understanding of satsang, namely that this satsang is of the soul and not of the physical body.

The final section of this memorable event was enjoyed with great vigour as the youths placed tokens on the scales weighing Shri Harikrishna Maharaj as they passed Swamishri for his darshan. The sadhus performed a series of lively kirtans, to the accompaniment of rhythmic beats of the drum, and ecstatic youths danced with joy around Swamishri. The pride discussed in such detail by Swamishri was emanating in abundance as the memorable occasion closed.

An old devotee had come for the darshan of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. While in government service he had done much seva for the organisation. Now, after retirement, an accident had left his leg disabled, and a feeling of inadequacy could be sensed in his heart: "Because of the disability in my leg I cannot do seva properly, and I keep feeling a certain incompleteness within."

On hearing this, Swamishri said, "Understand this feeling of incompleteness as God's grace. When one understands that one is incomplete, one is inspired to progress. If one believes oneself to be complete, one comes to a standstill. So do not worry that you feel incomplete. We have attained Maharaj and Swami, and they alone are going to liberate us. Until now you have been able to do seva, and you still do. You have firm faith in Akshar Purushottam, you have pleased Yogi Bapa, so nothing remains to be done. Understand that feeling incomplete is Maharaj's grace. Otherwise one would think, 'I have become complete and now I have nothing to do,' and one would become puffed up."
Who but the Satpurush can explain such intricacies of the path of spiritual practice?

Today, in the evening satsang assembly, in about 15 minutes of blessings, Pramukh Swami Maharaj spoke wonderfully about the understanding of satsang. After that Swamishri went into the lift to go to his residence. Referring to Swamishri's blessings today, a sadhu said, "Your system is truly something."
"How so?" Swamishri asked curiously.

"On one side, such heavy meetings go on about the organisation's many works, meetings in which there is not even time to breathe, and after coming here, as if there were nothing at all, to immediately and naturally speak so wonderfully, that can only be called being sthitapragna (of steady wisdom)!"
Hearing this, Swamishri said, "We speak remembering God. We speak as God makes us speak."
Swamishri spoke quite naturally. The line of Nishkulanand Swami, "Even without thinking, talks flow from his heart...", seemed to echo in everyone's heart!

Referring to Swamishri's blessings today, a sadhu said, "Your system is truly something." "Why?" Swamishri asked curiously. "On one side there are such heavy meetings about the many activities of the organisation, meetings where one does not get time even to breathe, and after coming here, as if there was nothing at all, you immediately and so naturally speak so wonderfully. That can only be called sthitapragnata (steadiness of wisdom)!"
Hearing this, Swamishri said, "We speak remembering God. We speak the way God makes us speak." Swamishri was speaking quite naturally.
The line of Nishkulanand Swami, "Even without thinking, words come from his heart...", seemed to echo in everyone's heart!

On Tuesday 3 May 2005, over 2,800 yuvatis from BAPS centers throughout Gujarat gathered at the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in Amdavad to participate in a special convention. Based on the theme 'BAPS-One Family' there were contributions by yuvatis from Amdavad, Vadodara, Rajkot, Bhuj, Bhavnagar and other centers. They presented speeches, devotional songs, discussions, traditional dances, skits and audio-visual shows on a wide variety of topics related to spirituality, personal development and everyday issues faced by yuvatis. There was also an interesting display of yoga. The chief guest of honor was the Gujarat State Education Minister, Shrimati Anandiben Patel. She was very pleased by the presence of so many enthusiastic yuvatis and offered some words of advice and encouragement to them. She felicitated 16 BAPS yuvatis who had attained significant success in various fields. The convention concluded with the yuvatis attending the evening satsang assembly in the presence of Pramukh Swami Maharaj.

Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha rituals of the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir, Junagadh. Thereafter at 10.05 am Swamishri attended the pratishtha assembly at the Agriculture University ground. Viveksagar Swami, Siddheshwar Swami, Dr Swami, and Mahant Swami addressed the assembly. The dignitaries on the dais were Shri Vajubhai Vala, President of BJP, Gujarat, city collector Shrimali, DIG Shri Mohan Jha, Commissioner Shri Meena, Vice-chancellor of Agriculture University Shri B.K. Kikani, DSP Shri Bhavsinh Vaghela, MLA Shri Kanubhai and Shri Devji-bhai who had helped in the acquisition of the mandir land. After the address of Shri Vaju-bhai Vala, Swamishri blessed the assembly.

Shri Amitabh Bachchan, the renowned film star, came for darshan of Thakorji and Swamishri at Dadar mandir. It was his second visit. Swamishri blessed him and gave him an abhishek murti of Shri Nilkanth Varni, a mala and tied a nada-chhadi on his wrist. Swamishri performed abhishek of the murti and told Shri Bachchan to perform abhishek, and also to do one mala daily. The next day he wrote of his meeting with Swamishri in his blog, “I had visited him earlier many years ago on a similar trip. A quiet, pious and soft spoken human. I had also visited the famous and grand Akshardham Temple complex in Delhi. An architectural wonder, run by devoted and disciplined Swamis. All of them working for equality and peace and education, following codes and principles that bring benefit to society. “Guruji spoke mostly in Gujarati, gave his blessings and various little tokens of affection and love for the family. I sat there humbled and silent. What does one say in the presence of divinity.”
